note: D-172. THIS IS A RATCHET, NOT AN EXCUSE. Every entry below is a check that is RED on integrate/first-usable today. None of them is fixed here and none of them is suppressed: each one still runs in full on every push to the integration branch and its findings are printed verbatim. What this file adds is the only thing a permanently-red step cannot give you -- a number that can FAIL. scripts/ci/quarantine-ratchet.mjs fails if a count goes UP (a regression slipped in) and also if a count goes DOWN without this file being lowered in the same change (a ratchet checked in one direction rots into a floor nobody ever lowers). Identical policy to scripts/ledger/state-baseline.json. To lower a number you must land the fix and the new number together.

notRatcheted.why: NOT ratcheted, and that is a finding rather than an omission. The check drives a real browser and measures horizontal overflow in pixels, so its finding count depends on the renderer: 6 blocking findings on WSL/Chromium (/docs/compare, /docs/download and /docs/faq at 320px and 390px @200%, overflow 8-81px) but 2 on ubuntu-latest/google-chrome (/docs/compare 320px by 18px, /docs/download 320px by 2px) -- measured on runs 30928896726 and 30929905893. Pinning either number produces a false red on the other machine. A ratchet whose value depends on which font stack is installed is not a ratchet. Recorded here so the finding is not lost and so nobody re-adds it to the ratchet without first making the measurement reproducible.
